title: Recertification Reasoning Framework v1
description: Creates a reusable, disease-agnostic, READ-ONLY, auditable period-over-period evidence-comparison framework -- NOT a recertification decision engine, NOT an eligibility engine, NOT a terminal-status engine, NOT a prognosis-prediction engine. Extends the merged Terminal Status Reasoning Framework v1 (PR #58) by adding benefit-period comparison semantics on top of PR #58's evidence sections, domain-to-section classification rules, evidence-strength vocabulary, and AI safety boundaries -- this manifest never duplicates any of that content. Defines the structural RECERTIFICATION_EVIDENCE_SUMMARY output (21 sections), a 9-label period-comparison vocabulary, two distinct regulatory-context definitions (federal CMS six-month hospice prognosis standard; California DPH hospice documentation/certification requirements) that are never combined or silently substituted for one another, 20 differentiation guards, and pure comparison functions (compare_scale, compare_numeric) for a future read-time API/AI layer. Creates zero patient facts, zero eligibility/terminal-status/prognosis/life-expectancy outputs, and zero certification/recertification/discharge recommendations. No schema changes. No migrations. No API changes. No changes to any prior PR's files.

new_disease.disease_description: A reusable, read-only container for the cross-disease, period-over-period RECERTIFICATION_EVIDENCE_SUMMARY reasoning framework: 21 section definitions plus a 9-label period-comparison vocabulary. Not a clinical disease and not a decision engine; hosts reference/classification metadata inside the existing Ontology Disease Blueprint schema without any migration. Extends, and never duplicates, the Terminal Status Reasoning Framework (PR #58).
new_disease.clinical_purpose: Gives physicians, medical directors, IDG members, and recertification/audit reviewers a single, consistent, source-traceable way to compare a patient's documented evidence between the immediately preceding benefit period and the current benefit period -- functional status, ADL/care dependence, nutrition/hydration, disease-specific findings, symptoms, labs, complications, utilization, treatment context, co-morbidities, stability/improvement, and potentially reversible factors -- while explicitly surfacing missing evidence, documentation gaps, and conflicting evidence for physician/medical-director review, without ever generating an eligibility, terminal-status, prognosis, or recertification conclusion itself.
new_disease.hospice_relevance: CMS terminal-status guidance requires the record to support the physician's clinical judgment through documented comparison over time; diagnosis alone is insufficient and baseline guidelines do not independently qualify a patient. California hospice regulations separately require consistent outcome measurement, comprehensive written assessments, evaluation of change since the previous assessment, and authenticated, traceable documentation. This framework supports both regulatory contexts as clinical review material only -- it never determines eligibility, terminal status, prognosis, or recertification, and never replaces attending-physician or medical-director judgment.

regulatory_context_definitions.prognosis_standard: Six-month terminal prognosis if the illness runs its normal course
regulatory_context_definitions.notes: The federal Medicare hospice terminal-status review uses the six-month prognosis standard reflected in the CMS LCD materials. This context must never be silently substituted for, or combined with, the California state context.

regulatory_context_definitions.prognosis_standard: Not a distinct prognosis-period standard -- separate state certification and documentation requirements (outcome measurement, comprehensive assessments, reassessment of response to care, authenticated and traceable record entries)
regulatory_context_definitions.notes: California hospice regulations impose distinct documentation and record-keeping requirements. This context is preserved separately and must never overwrite or be merged with the federal Medicare six-month standard.

framework_sections.section_description: Patient/episode/benefit-period identifiers, documented primary and secondary diagnoses (never inferred), regulatory authority/jurisdiction/payer context, applicable disease blueprint, and framework/manifest version metadata.

The most relevant documented prior-period evidence across every comparison category, each retaining its original source reference. Reports PRIOR_BASELINE_MISSING when no prior-period value exists; never treats a missing prior value as decline.

Current documented evidence using the same categories and normalization rules as the prior-period baseline. Undated evidence is never treated as current evidence -- it is routed to Section 18 (Documentation Gaps).

Like-for-like scale comparison only (PPS-to-PPS, KPS-to-KPS, ECOG-to-ECOG, FAST-to-FAST, NYHA-to-NYHA); never cross-scale. Reports scale type, prior/current value and date, direction, and source references using each scale's own ordering.

Compares documented dependence for feeding, ambulation, continence, transfer, bathing, dressing, supervision/cueing needs, caregiver assistance, dependent-ADL count, increasing care needs, bedbound/chairbound status. Never infers ADL dependence from diagnosis or functional score alone.

Compares documented weight, calculable percentage weight change, mid-arm circumference, abdominal girth, oral intake, meal percentage, diet consistency, swallowing/dysphagia/aspiration, hydration status, albumin/cholesterol, artificial nutrition/hydration, refusal, and treatment limitations. Flags documented potentially-reversible causes rather than automatically attributing change to disease progression.

Uses only the active disease blueprint(s) matching documented primary/secondary diagnoses; never applies one disease's criteria to another. Reports newly documented, no-longer-documented, unchanged, conflicting, and missing disease-specific evidence with source references.

Compares documented trends in dyspnea, cough, pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, weakness, fatigue, edema, ascites, altered level of consciousness, and disease-specific symptom burden/frequency/severity/treatment responsiveness. Never infers severity from medication orders alone.

Compares only documented lab/objective values with compatible units; never invents equivalent units or requires testing the governing LCD marks optional. Reports test name, prior/current value+unit+date, source reference, and unit-compatibility status.

Tracks documented complications/infections with event date, source, treatment response, and recurrence status. Never treats a historical complication as current without current documentation of persistence or recurrence.

Compares documented ED visits, observation stays, admissions, readmissions, physician visits, and urgent calls, with date/type/reason/related-diagnosis/source. Never automatically classifies unrelated utilization as advanced-disease progression.

Documents changes in disease-directed/palliative treatment, oxygen/ventilation/artificial nutrition-hydration/dialysis, transplant status, surgical candidacy, refusal, intolerance, and treatment failure. Never interprets refusal as incapacity, never infers failure without documentation, and never recommends any treatment action.

Lists documented active co-morbidities with severity evidence, current treatment context, and a contribution-status label. Never infers contribution solely from the co-morbidity's existence and never converts co-morbidity count into a score.

Explicitly surfaces every stable or improving domain -- never hidden. Reports prior/current state, dates, sources, documented explanation, and whether improvement may be temporary, plus a physician-review question. Never treats stability as automatic ineligibility nor continued decline elsewhere as automatic eligibility.

Identifies documented factors that may explain decline but may be reversible (e.g. acute infection under treatment, medication effect, dehydration). Never determines reversibility itself -- routes the issue to physician review.

Detects and displays contradictions (e.g. inconsistent PPS on the same date, conflicting weight values) without resolving them automatically. Every conflict retains type, involved values, dates, source-record identifiers, and a physician-review prompt; resolution status starts UNRESOLVED.
Identifies expected evidence categories with no usable documented evidence. Missing evidence means DOCUMENTATION NOT FOUND -- it must never mean the clinical condition is absent.

Identifies evidence that exists but is not sufficiently usable (no date/assessor/source, ambiguous units, copied-forward content, conflicting values, unsigned/unauthenticated entries, generic narrative language, unsupported conclusions, untraceable corrections).
Generates patient-specific review questions only, derived from identified evidence or gaps -- never generates answers or conclusions.

Generates individualized narrative elements (not a completed certification) drawn from documented, source-traceable evidence. Never creates a physician attestation or signature, never states hospice status, eligibility, or life expectancy, never recommends certification/recertification, and every element must be labeled as AI-generated, never as physician-authored.

Every summarized evidence item carries evidence_id, patient/episode/benefit-period references, disease/domain/concept identity, exact documented value and unit, assessment/documentation dates, source-record identifiers, framework_version, classification_rule_id, generated_at, and read_only=true. Distinguishes source clinical facts from framework classifications and AI-generated prompts/narrative suggestions; generated output never masquerades as clinician-authored documentation.

on_missing_immediately_preceding_period: do not silently skip to an older period
optionally display older evidence under HISTORICAL_CONTEXT, explicitly labeled
never combine evidence from multiple periods into one undocumented baseline

comparison_vocabulary.disclaimer: These labels describe DOCUMENTED CHANGE ONLY. They never describe eligibility, terminal status, prognosis, certification, or coverage.

labels.label: DECLINING
labels.definition: Documented current value/state reflects worse function or greater burden than the documented prior value/state, per the concept's own ordering.

labels.label: STABLE
labels.definition: Documented current value/state is unchanged from the documented prior value/state.

labels.label: IMPROVING
labels.definition: Documented current value/state reflects better function or lesser burden than the documented prior value/state, per the concept's own ordering.

labels.label: MIXED
labels.definition: Some sub-elements of a comparison category improved while others declined; reported explicitly rather than averaged.

labels.label: INDETERMINATE
labels.definition: Both prior and current values are documented and dated but do not support a clear directional conclusion.

labels.label: NOT_APPLICABLE
labels.definition: The comparison category does not apply to this patient/disease/scale combination.

labels.label: PRIOR_VALUE_MISSING
labels.definition: No dated prior-period value exists for this concept -- a documentation-completeness flag, never treated as decline.

labels.label: CURRENT_VALUE_MISSING
labels.definition: No dated current-period value exists for this concept -- a documentation-completeness flag only.

labels.label: CONFLICTING_DOCUMENTATION
labels.definition: Prior and/or current values conflict across source records for the same concept and date; the framework never resolves which source is correct.

evidence_completeness_vocabulary_referen.note: This manifest never redefines or duplicates the PR #58 evidence-strength vocabulary. It is referenced by name only; the four labels remain documentation-completeness labels, never weighted scores, points, probabilities, risk percentages, or patient rankings.

physician_review_prompts: What documented changes since the prior benefit period support the current clinical prognosis?
How does the current functional status compare with the prior benefit-period baseline?
What disease-specific findings remain active and clinically significant?
How do current nutritional, hydration, and swallowing findings affect the clinical picture?
How do recent hospitalizations or exacerbations relate to the documented advanced condition?
What is the clinical significance of documented stability or improvement?
Are potentially reversible causes contributing to the observed decline?
How do active co-morbidities contribute to the current prognosis?
Which conflicting findings require clarification before completing the narrative?
narrative_support_elements: Current primary diagnosis and relevant secondary diagnoses.

ai_may: identify potentially reversible factors for review

unsupported_content_not_created: Any per-concept OntologyRelationship edge linking every existing disease concept to a comparison section (deliberately out of scope, same rationale as PR #58).
Any patient-fact table, row, insert, update, or delete of any kind -- this manifest creates only its own 22 framework registry concepts.
Any eligibility, terminal-status, prognosis, or life-expectancy output of any kind.
Any certification, recertification, or discharge recommendation of any kind.
A duplicate copy of PR #58's 11 evidence sections, classification_rules, or evidence-strength vocabulary -- referenced by name only.
Any new disease-specific clinical concept, threshold, or scale.
